title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems

details.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
details.abstract: Decision models support routing, guardrails, and output verification in LLM systems. However, item accuracy alone cannot establish whether models make correct decisions across controlled variations or assign reliable confidence to their predictions. We introduce DecisionPivot, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 48 tasks and 40,033 items across seven decision roles. Its core track contains 7,800 items from 13 generated task families, organized into contrast groups with computed answers verified by independently implemented solvers. The complementary reference track contains 32,233 items from 35 public test sets, preserving their original evaluation metrics. We evaluate 40 decision models and 14 general models using documented, model-specific protocols, assessing item and contrast-group accuracy, probability ordering, calibration, and empirical selective coverage. Our results reveal substantial differences obscured by aggregate scores: two 27B models separated by only 2.6 points on the reference track achieve contrast-group accuracies of 70.1% and 44.2%. Across 2,400 binary contrast pairs, Perplexity Decider correctly ranks the positive member above the negative member in 92.3% of pairs but answers both members correctly in only 74.1%, exposing a gap between probability ordering and decision correctness. Models with similar item accuracy also differ in the reliability of their high-confidence predictions. On a separate 1,296-item subset, GLM-5.3 achieves 93.5% contrast-group accuracy at a higher reasoning setting, compared with 81.5% at its lowest effort. By linking errors to pivotal details and difficulty levels, DecisionPivot provides fine-grained diagnostics of decision failures that aggregate evaluation alone cannot reveal.

title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research

details.title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research
details.abstract: We present Épi, an autonomous research agent that sustains investigations across model sessions and evolves its methods through accumulated experience. Épi combines persistent research history, hierarchical memory, branching and independent review to maintain research continuity, learn from experiments, and explore and revisit alternative approaches. Its experiments run across session boundaries, and a fixed verifier evaluates their outputs. Épi produced 120 record-setting results, comprising 20 numerical bound records across 12 families and 100 construction records across eight families. These include an approximately 84-fold narrower interval for the n-queens constant and a more than 3.6-million-fold narrower rigorous interval for the quartic Feigenbaum attractor dimension. Exact dual certificates establish that the Cohn-Elkies linear-programming bound cannot be sharp in dimensions 10 and 11. Beyond numerical improvements, Épi gives a computer-assisted proof of Tuza's conjecture for split graphs with an eight-vertex clique part and at most three triangle-active neighborhood types, with arbitrary multiplicities. We extend this research process to algorithmic coding with Épi-turbo, a lightweight configuration that develops executable solvers for tasks including vehicle routing, scheduling and production planning. On 30 FrontierOR tasks, Épi-turbo achieves a 5.4% higher total benchmark score than Codex at 64% of its model cost, using the same underlying model and reasoning effort. Épi is designed to support human understanding by connecting computational results to explicit methods and mathematical arguments that researchers can examine and build upon.

title: FlowState: Execution State as Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

details.title: FlowState: Execution State as Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
details.abstract: We explore how long-horizon LLM agents can preserve useful information without repeatedly loading their entire interaction history. FlowState maintains structured execution states linked to original tool observations, updates them as tasks progress, and retrieves relevant states and evidence on demand. Using the same DeepSeek-V4-Flash backbone, FlowState improves average success rate on MemoryArena by 4.55 percentage points and average pass rate on τ³-Bench by 13.95 percentage points over a full-context baseline, while reducing total token consumption by 43.2% and 40.6%, respectively. We welcome questions and feedback, especially on agent memory and long-horizon task execution!

title: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success

details.title: Good Judgment, Bad Advice: Decision-Model Controllers Raise Agent Cost Without Improving Success
details.abstract: Can a specialized decision model make AI agents more efficient, or does it just add overhead? We investigate whether delegating decisions like when to stop, verify, or change approach to a specialized decision model improves agent performance. Using Terminal-Bench 2.1, we compare five controller strategies within the same agent loop: no controller, deterministic rules, a small LLM, Jev 1.13, and a placebo controller. Key findings: 19% higher cost per attempt with Jev, without improving task success (73% vs. 73%). Jev showed stronger offline finish-decision discrimination (AUROC 0.78) than rules (0.62) or a small LLM (0.60). Despite better offline decision signals, calibration challenges contributed to unnecessary verification and additional overhead. Our findings suggest that better decision-making in isolation does not necessarily translate into better end-to-end agent performance. Controller calibration, intervention timing, and cost all matter. The study includes 315 trials across 21 held-out tasks , with code released for reproducibility. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24649 Curious whether others have observed similar trade-offs when introducing specialized decision models into agent workflows.

title: HarnessRL: Co-Evolving Policies with a Just-in-Time Training Harness for Open-Ended RL

details.title: HarnessRL: Co-Evolving Policies with a Just-in-Time Training Harness for Open-Ended RL
details.abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning enables open-ended generation using natural-language criteria as rewards, but these signals can become ineffective as the policy evolves. We identify two failure modes: non-discriminative rewards, where scores collapse to uniformly low or high values due to insufficient exploration or a mismatch between task difficulty and policy capability, and spurious rewards, where higher scores do not correspond to better responses. Both reflect a fixed training configuration that fails to adapt as the policy evolves, including what to train on, how to explore, and how to evaluate. We introduce HarnessRL, a training-time harness that co-evolves with the policy through three interfaces: task sampling, rollout guidance, and rubric criteria. HarnessRL maintains a training-time memory that retrieves within-task history and cross-task evidence. A harness evolver uses this evidence to attribute each reward failure to the interface whose update can address it, then runs a proposer and just-in-time critic loop in which the critic accepts a candidate update only after measuring its effect on the current frozen policy. We further introduce Rubric-Mix-10k, a unified five-domain training and evaluation suite for open-ended RL spanning medical, science, writing, role-playing, and instruction-following tasks. On Rubric-Mix-10k, HarnessRL outperforms the strongest baselines by 2.8 to 3.1 points across both 4B and 9B model scales and nearly halves the training steps to its best checkpoint.

Given text and a rig, JCA generates video together with 3D motion that responds to the surrounding scene. It also recovers the camera, allowing the animation to be placed and replayed in the 3D scene. Beyond text-driven generation, it supports video-to-motion, motion-to-video, and keyframe control of the 3D motion. Explore the videos and results: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/

title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents

details.title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence in LLM Agents
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 Can more memory make an LLM agent worse? We study error reproduction: mistakes in stored rules or skills can shape future executions, which then produce new abstractions that regenerate the same mistakes. We propose Anti-Persistence: retain trajectories and outcomes, but reconstruct task-specific guidance on demand and discard it after execution. An adaptive selector decides whether and how to generate this guidance. Across the benchmarks and models we evaluated, Anti-Persistence achieves higher overall held-out success and the lowest average LLM-call cost among the compared memory designs. Our takeaway: accumulating experience and permanently storing its interpretations are separate design choices. We’d love to hear your experiences with agent memory and recurring errors. Happy to answer questions!

title: Large Flow Language Models

details.title: Large Flow Language Models
details.abstract: Continuous flow language models offer a path to parallel generation with tools for control and acceleration unavailable to discrete diffusion, yet effective techniques for building them at the billion-parameter scale remain less established. We present Lafa (Large flow language model), a fast, high-performing flow language model scaled to 8B parameters in a data-efficient manner. Lafa is a blockwise flow model with causal attention on the prefix and bidirectional, asynchronous flow within each block. This design enables efficient training by adapting pretrained autoregressive (AR) models and fast inference via prefix caching and blockwise parallel decoding. We train Lafa at 0.5B, 7B, and 8B scales with fewer than 30B tokens, more efficient than previous diffusion models, and evaluate it on instruction following, reasoning, and coding, where the learned flow matches or surpasses the quality of AR and can be distilled into flow maps for one- and few-step generation. Notably, flow training preserves or even improves pretrained AR capabilities via a multi-token prediction effect, which we leverage in a self-speculative decoding scheme that verifies flow-based drafts autoregressively within a single model. This yields 2.54x the throughput of an AR model at comparable quality, outperforming multi-token prediction and discrete diffusion methods. Our findings show that continuous flows can serve as a scalable foundation for language modeling.

details.abstract: Hi everyone! First author here 👋 Can an agent become more reliable by improving its harness while keeping model weights fixed? We introduce RiseHarness, a framework for iterative harness self-evolution. It studies tasks where the same agent sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails, combining agent trajectories with internal harness traces to understand what went wrong. A Harness Handbook connects these findings to source code, enabling targeted changes informed by implementations from other agent frameworks. Each proposed change goes through behavioral checks and repeated evaluation, with measured improvements carried into the next iteration. title: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Before Post-Training: An End-to-End Approach

details.title: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Before Post-Training: An End-to-End Approach
details.abstract: Agentic capabilities are increasingly important for modern LLMs, yet remain difficult to evaluate during pretraining. Existing approaches typically rely on static trajectory-derived tasks or likelihood-based proxies, which are lightweight but provide limited visibility into how base models behave in interactive environments. We introduce ASAP (Agent Scaffold Adaptation for Pretraining Evaluation), a lightweight framework for eliciting and evaluating agentic behavior from pretrained base models on end-to-end tasks. Rather than converting base models into chat-style agents, ASAP preserves the completion interface and adapts existing agent scaffolds through structured trajectory continuation, short reference prefixes, and minimal recovery mechanisms. Across software-engineering and deep-research benchmarks, ASAP yields discriminative end-to-end performance across base models and pretraining checkpoints. Beyond aggregate scores, ASAP exposes model-generated execution trajectories, enabling analysis of exploration, editing, testing, recovery, and task completion across training stages. These trajectories provide a behavioral view of how agent-relevant capabilities change during pretraining and how execution patterns differ after post-training. Our results suggest that end-to-end agent evaluation can complement conventional pretraining benchmarks by providing a practical diagnostic of interactive model behavior.

title: WinARDet: Compressed Window Auto-Regression for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Grounding

details.title: WinARDet: Compressed Window Auto-Regression for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Grounding
details.abstract: MLLM-based detectors formulate vision-language grounding as autoregressive coordinate generation, yet in dense scenes, they often collapse into a box repetition loop, repeatedly emitting identical boxes until the decoding budget is exhausted. We trace this failure to historical-answer attention takeover: Under full-history autoregression, repeated coordinate tokens in the growing answer history attract disproportionate attention, crowding out the attention sinks needed to attend to new visual evidence. To break this loop, in this paper, we propose Compressed Window Auto-Regression (WinAR). This new mechanism partitions a long answer sequence into consecutive generation windows and restricts full token-level autoregression to the current window only while compressing each previous window into a fixed set of latent tokens that condition subsequent decoding. This design reduces the repeated exposure to raw historical coordinates that triggers the attention takeover, yet preserves cross-window dependencies essential for coherent multi-object generation. On RSDense, which contains 200-2,000 objects per image, our model WinARDet improves RexOmni F1-score (IoU=0.5) from 32.16 to 39.36 over the baseline, while reducing the redundancy rate from 35.48% to 13.00%. WinARDet also generalizes across decoding strategies and output formats, including parallel box decoding and polygon generation, providing a practical paradigm for long-horizon vision-language grounding across scene densities.

title: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements

details.title: PVBench: Quantifying Physical Plausibility in Video Generation with Object-Level Physical Measurements
details.abstract: PVBench is a benchmark and toolkit for evaluating the physical plausibility of AI-generated videos. It aims to systematically assess whether object motion, spatial relationships, material changes, causal behavior, and mechanical laws depicted in videos are physically reasonable. The benchmark covers seven domains—instruction and semantic fidelity, behavior and causality, perceptual quality, geometry and space, material properties, kinematics and temporal persistence, and mechanics and conservation—and comprises 46 evaluation dimensions. It also includes 600 evaluation scenarios, 30% of which involve embodied agents such as robots. By combining quantitative physical metrics with multimodal large language model-assisted evaluation, PVBench provides a comprehensive evaluation framework for video-generation models and helps move AI-generated video from “looking realistic” toward “truly obeying the laws of physics.”

Each frequency band is forecast on its own clock, and the transformer runs only when the forecast becomes too uncertain, achieving high speedup while preserving generation quality.

title: PhysLDM: Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Deformable Simulation

details.title: PhysLDM: Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Deformable Simulation
details.abstract: What if physics simulation worked like video generation? 🎬 PhysLDM is a latent diffusion paradigm for high-fidelity deformable simulation: a single model predicts an entire trajectory of a high-resolution soft body at once and generalizes zero-shot. 🔑 Highlights: High-fidelity spatiotemporal VAE : Video-VAE-style temporal compression causes "staircase" artifacts. We propose a holistic ST-VAE that decouples rigid motion from deformation: ~2.48 mm geometric reconstruction precision on meter-scale scenes at up to 78× token compression. Regression vs. diffusion : Complex deformable dynamics are often chaotic: even a GPU solver ends in clearly different states from identical inputs. In this regime deterministic regression collapses toward damped, non-physical averages, while diffusion models the distribution. Strong zero-shot generalization : Trained purely kinematically on Objaverse-scale simulations, a single PhysLDM transfers zero-shot to OOD datasets (GSO, Toys4K). Its ST-VAE also zero-shot reconstructs an unseen energy model (4.6 mm) and real-world data (6.0 mm) accurately. Differentiable, unlocking hard inverse problems : With end-to-end and higher-order gradients, PhysLDM efficiently and accurately recovers Young's modulus from a single trajectory, and solves second-order design tasks that are prohibitive for existing differentiable simulators. 🌐 Project page: https://yucrazing.github.io/physldm/ 🐦 X: https://x.com/yucrazing/status/2112180645736952267?s=20

title: On the Limits of Scale: Inverse Scaling in Vision-Language Models

details.title: On the Limits of Scale: Inverse Scaling in Vision-Language Models
details.abstract: In this paper, we investigate does scaling a vision-language model improve every capability. We compare 19 open-weight VLMs (Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5, Gemma 3, Molmo 2; 1B to 241B) on 8 benchmarks, comparing smaller and larger models on the same questions. We find 375 subtask-level inverse-scaling cases. Thirteen subtasks regress in at least three independent families, and the effect survives dense-only and twofold-size restrictions, statistical correction and annotation audits. Chain-of-thought helps on knowledge-heavy tasks, but about half of the perception cases persist. Takeaway: evaluate different size of models on your VLM task, the biggest model may not necessarily be the best one for it.

title: Cache Engineering for Agents

details.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
details.abstract: We let agents manage their KV cache directly, proactively dropping what they no longer need without rewriting their conversation history or recomputing the remaining cache. We built AKV serving system to support this efficiently, reducing cache for long-running agents.

title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?

details.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
details.abstract: Can VLM agents actively explore a scene and build an accurate 3D map? 🧭 We introduce SpatialScout, a benchmark for evaluating VLM agents on active object-level 3D mapping across 80 diverse indoor scenes. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, and camera calibration and poses, agents must control a camera, gather visual evidence, and estimate object centers in a shared 3D coordinate frame. 🔍 What does SpatialScout test? Active exploration: choosing informative viewpoints under limited interaction budgets. Spatial mapping: associating objects across views and progressively refining their 3D positions. Accuracy and completeness: evaluating localization while penalizing missing objects. 📊 Precise mapping remains challenging: the strongest evaluated model achieves 41.71% mean IoU, with only 3.25% of targets exceeding IoU 0.9. Our results reveal a substantial gap between recovering coarse object layouts and building complete, precise metric maps. 💬 We welcome feedback and discussion on active perception and spatial intelligence! 💻 Code: https://github.com/JesseZZZZZ/SpatialScout

title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models

details.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
details.abstract: TL;DR: We introduce StreamEval, the first benchmark for interactive streaming video generation . It evaluates whether models can handle incrementally arriving multimodal requests while executing specified state changes and preserving content throughout an ongoing stream. Benchmark: 300 scripted test cases lasting 15 to 300 seconds, with defined initial assets and timed interaction requirements across five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. Findings: Strong visual quality and identity retention do not necessarily coincide with reliable request execution or sustained state consistency. The highest Following scores are 36.90 for avatar performance and 25.93 for text conditioned world generation. Executing requests under timing and preservation constraints remains a central challenge for real time omnimodal interactive systems. 💻 Code: https://github.com/StreamEval/StreamEval 🎬 Data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/StreamEval/StreamEval 🏠 Leaderboard: https://streameval.ai

title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis

details.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
details.abstract: We introduce WildAWM (Agent World Model in the Wild), a scalable pipeline that synthesizes executable computer-use agent (CUA) environments and tasks for training general CUA, powered entirely by open-source models. Core contributions: Worlds: persona-driven, multi-day personal computers where websites, MCP services, and local files share one state, so agents can combine GUI, MCP, and CLI, and the whole pipeline is powered by open-source models, without any reliance on proprietary frontier models. Tasks: execution-based quality gates (heterogeneous agent rollouts, cross-judge consistency checks, and counterfactual probes) keep tasks solvable, challenging, and reliably verified. We release 341 environment–task pairs; some need over 100 agent steps, and GPT-6-Astra solves only about 60%. Results: trained exclusively in these synthetic worlds, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-4B improve on all 8 out-of-distribution benchmarks spanning web, claw, and computer-use agents, by +10.58 and +8.21 points on average. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26828 Project page: https://msr-orchard.github.io/WildAWM/ GitHub: https://github.com/MSR-Orchard/WildAWM Data & models: https://huggingface.co/collections/ChilleD/agent-world-model-in-the-wild Harbor dataset: https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/wildawm

title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation

details.title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation
details.abstract: 🔥🔥🔥Which spectral channels matter, and where? SSI explains a model score with signed attributions for each spatial cell and channel. It keeps the surrounding image fixed while allocating a cell's contribution among its channels using Shapley values. A channel's contribution can change across an image. SSI asks how the channels within one spatial cell affect the chosen model score, conditioned on the observed values of all other cells. ✅ SSI has the best reported mean for all three metrics on all three datasets under both masking baselines. For example, mean-baseline HLS joint deletion is .1545 for SSI versus .2096 for KernelSHAP, the strongest non-SSI method on that metric. ✅ SSI leads the compared methods in spatial localization, spectral Hit@K, and channel deletion across the evaluated datasets.

title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations

details.title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations
details.abstract: DONIC is a generalist dexterous bimanual tracking policy: one policy learns to track diverse human two-hand demonstrations with two robot hands, and generalizes to unseen trajectories and unseen objects without fine-tuning . 🔥 Highlights 🤲 Policy — One Policy, Two Hands. A single reference-conditioned policy controls two Wuji dexterous hands and tracks bimanual references across operation categories and human-motion sources. 📊 Data — BiHOI. 1,575 multi-view bimanual sequences over 229 objects and 14.77 hours of interaction, captured with a calibrated multi-view camera array and emphasizing sustained two-hand contact. 🧠 Learning — Signals Built for Two Hands. An object-centered per-hand reward, Clip-Centered Advantages, and a PPO + behavioral cloning loop that recycles replay-verified successful executions into training demonstrations. 🏆 Generalization — Zero Fine-Tuning. 86.79% success on unseen trajectories and 57.32% on unseen objects in simulation, 77.36 and 45.73 percentage points above the stronger of our bimanual adaptations of DexTrack and Dexplore. 📈 Scaling — More Human Data Helps. Adding BiHOI improves all seven metrics on both held-out splits, raising success to 88.68% and 59.76%.

title: Socratic Skill Learning: Interleaving Teaching and Practice for Transferable Agent Skills

details.title: Socratic Skill Learning: Interleaving Teaching and Practice for Transferable Agent Skills
details.abstract: Agent Skills improve LLM agents by making task knowledge reusable across sessions. Learning transferable Skills requires evidence about a procedure and its conditions of use, which a successful task attempt can leave untested. We introduce Socratic Skill Learning (SSL), which interleaves expert teaching with Student practice. An Educator guides investigation while the Student remains the sole environment operator and Skill author, able to question, test, and adapt advice. To test reuse beyond the learning task, we construct SKILLTRANSFERBENCH, with 35 task families and 408 executable cases, pairing public variation specifications with held-out evaluation in fresh solver sessions. On the main 22-family, 155-case cohort, Fixed-Window SSL reaches 0.801 utility, versus 0.723 without a Skill, 0.761 for adapted Trace2Skill (trajectory distillation), and 0.751 for adapted SKILL-KD (contrastive distillation). Across three model pairs on shared families, interleaved guidance outperforms expert authoring and post-hoc teaching. Process analysis links guidance to Student writing and package revision; a case study shows the Student testing and refining a proposed procedure for later reuse. As demand for new lessons falls, the cost of fixed-window review grows. Issue-Guided SSL tracks unresolved questions across Skill revisions to select and focus review, reaching 0.805 utility with 61.7% fewer Educator tokens and 16.9% fewer total acquisition tokens than Fixed-Window SSL on the main cohort

title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics

details.title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
details.abstract: AgenticRoboRL trains the planner model of a robot harness inside the harness itself. A harness pairs a language model planner with robot tools: the planner may call a VLA policy as a skill, or write Python against the harness's robot APIs. The harness keeps its tools and its control loop, and only the planner is trained. SFT on a stronger teacher's successful trajectories, each turn rendered as the request the student would receive. Multi-turn RL with the simulator's success verdict as the reward. Rollouts run in the harness, and a proxy between the harness and the model server records every planner call with its token ids and log-probabilities. One pipeline for different harnesses. A harness is connected through a short adapter that reports which episodes form a group and how each one ended. This repository connects two harnesses, one that calls a VLA policy (RPent) and one that generates control code (CaP-X). We introduce PAPAV — Perceive, Anticipate, Plan, Act, Verify — a capability-centric framework for understanding Multimodal Embodied Agents across digital and physical interaction. Our analysis of 64 benchmarks reveals a clear gap: evaluation is heavily concentrated on Act , while Anticipate and Verify remain largely underexplored. We hope this survey provides a unified map of the emerging Agent + Robot landscape and a useful basis for future research.

title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers

details.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
details.abstract: We introduce ALLOT, a training-free sparsity allocation method for block-sparse attention in video Diffusion Transformers. Our approach estimates each layer–step cell’s final-video sensitivity and jointly allocates densities under a measured-latency budget. At matched or shorter wall-clock time, it achieves an 11.8 dB PSNR gain over XAttention’s default on HunyuanVideo and outperforms or ties the defaults in all nine settings across four additional published pipelines.

title: DeLoop: Repeated Actions as Self-Supervision for Long-Horizon Agents

details.title: DeLoop: Repeated Actions as Self-Supervision for Long-Horizon Agents
details.abstract: TL DR: LLM agents often re-issue a tool call they already made and get the same observation back. We call this a loop . DeLoop turns each loop into a free training pair from the agent's own rollout: the repeated call is the rejected action, and the agent's first later loop-breaking action is the chosen one. We train on these pairs with DPO. No task reward, gold answer, or LLM judge needed. Why it matters: loops get much worse when the history is compressed. On CodeGym, Qwen3-8B loops in 29.0% of runs with the full history and in 57.3% under summarization. Summaries that explicitly track past actions don't fix it, because the agent often ignores a record it already has. Results Qwen3-8B on CodeGym: loop rate 57.3% → 6.1% (9.4×), steps per task 15.0 → 4.7 , tokens −47%, with similar task success Qwen3-14B / 32B: task success +7.2 / +7.1 points (45.1 → 52.3 , 37.7 → 44.8 ) With cross-domain pairs (DeLoop-Mix): Qwen3-8B success 25.1 → 30.3 . Loops also drop under 7 memory policies, in ALFWorld, Open-AgentRL, AppWorld, ScienceWorld, and BrowseComp-Plus (22.4% → 1.2%) 🔗 Project page (with an interactive example of a loop forming): https://cskyl.github.io/deloop/ 📄 arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19376 💻 Code and data: coming soon at https://github.com/cskyl/deloop

title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models

details.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
details.abstract: World models often predict and plan over the tokens of a frozen visual encoder, so the encoder determines what they can see. We introduce ALPS (A Language-aligned, Pixel-renderable State encoder), a ViT-B/16 pretrained from scratch using only still images and text. A single set of frozen patch tokens supports physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction . We first establish language, pixel, and spatial capabilities through joint pretraining, then strengthen state representations via cross-view self-distillation. Key results: State: Lowest aggregate LIBERO state-probe error among ViT-B encoders (compared with 15 public encoders), matching the 3.5× larger V-JEPA 2-L. Language: Strong native language alignment, achieving 93.2% Flickr30k and 70.2% COCO image-to-text Recall@1. Pixels: Accurate pixel reconstruction from frozen tokens, including direct rendering of predicted world-model futures. Control & Planning: Highest mean LIBERO policy success (85.5%) with its native text tower; matches or exceeds leading encoders on PushT, Wall, and Granular. Open release: Both checkpoints (Stage 1 & ALPS), eight LIBERO policies, and JAX / PyTorch training and evaluation code. 🌐 Project: https://ucsc-vlaa.github.io/ALPS/ 💻 Code: https://github.com/UCSC-VLAA/ALPS 🤗 Weights: https://huggingface.co/UCSC-VLAA/ALPS

title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States

details.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
details.abstract: We propose a new quantizer and also a new way on how to quantize states in linear-attention-based layers in language models. As the actual state is not materialized in the kernels for every token step, but at a chunk size, we can also adapt the number of rounding. This gives headroom for lower precision states and also aligns well with kv buffering methods during decoding.

title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning

details.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
details.abstract: Excited to share our work Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning ! Most existing agentic RL methods train through a single fixed harness, potentially limiting generalization across different execution configurations. We introduce Harness Scaling , a new scaling dimension for agentic RL that focuses on how agents execute , complementing traditional scaling over tasks and environments. Our approach organizes harness diversity through five components (system prompt, tool interface, observation, context management, and workflow), combining structured configuration selection with cross-harness RL. Key findings: Harness Scaling consistently improves generalization to unseen harness configurations across models, benchmarks, and RL algorithms. Structured harness selection and locality-aware training are more effective than simply increasing the number of training configurations. Remarkably, training across diverse white-box harnesses transfers effectively to unseen black-box harnesses such as Claude Code, even outperforming direct black-box RL training. Our results highlight that not only harness diversity, but how it is organized, matters for generalizable agentic RL. Feedback and discussions are very welcome!

title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams

details.title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
details.abstract: 🚀 We present GRSE (Group-Relative Skill Evolution), a framework that tackles a fundamental question in multi-agent learning: When a team succeeds or fails, which agent's skill should actually change? Instead of rewarding all skills involved in successful trajectories, GRSE performs group-relative credit assignment across multiple executions to identify the skills that truly drive outcomes. Key highlights: 🎯 Assigns credit at the agent-skill level 🔍 Identifies causal contributors through trajectory comparison 🤝 Supports continual multi-agent skill evolution 📈 Outperforms existing skill-learning methods on HotpotQA and LoCoMo 🛡️ Remains robust under noisy and corrupted skill libraries We believe GRSE is an important step toward scalable and self-improving multi-agent systems. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27227 💻 Code: https://github.com/yananma1029/GRSE-Skills

title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience

details.title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
details.abstract: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. The key distinction is between evidence about a scene and experience about how to reason with that evidence. 3DFusionMemory fuses current-scene observations into queryable spatial relations. A Spatial Skill Library provides reusable tool procedures, and Spatial Cognition associates task conditions with experience about when and how to use memory and skills. Completed trajectories are abstracted into process records and consolidated between task blocks, allowing later decisions to draw on earlier execution without transferring scene coordinates or reference answers. Across five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, SpatialBrain improves on direct answers from the same backbone on four and ties on the fifth. Component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions characterize how the framework accumulates and uses these resources.

title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation

details.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
details.abstract: 🧠 Every interaction gets the same compute. Should it? Introducing LoopRec , from our paper Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation . We explore a simple idea: let each historical item learn how deeply it needs to be processed. 🔍 The evidence behind adaptive depth In a three-layer SASRec diagnostic on Amazon Office, 76.14% of items stabilize after one layer, while 6.72% require all three. Shallow and deep computational needs coexist within the same history. 🔁 One shared block, different depths LoopRec reuses a weight-shared backbone block recursively. Lightweight gates decide, item by item, whether to exit or continue—without auxiliary depth labels. Learned routing allocates deeper computation to rarer items and more recent interactions. 📈 Consistent gains across architectures Across 3 Amazon benchmarks × 4 backbones —SASRec, BSARec, NextItNet, and LRURec—all 48 reported ranking comparisons improve; 44 are statistically significant. On Patio, NextItNet's NDCG@20 rises from 0.0192 to 0.0263 (+37.02%) . 💡 Adaptive computation opens a promising direction for recommendation: learning where additional depth is useful within each user's history. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30128 💻 Code: https://github.com/Elpmis117/LoopRec We'd love to hear your thoughts on adaptive depth for recommender systems! 🤗

title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally

details.title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally
details.abstract: When a speaker says ``some students passed'', listeners infer that not all of them did. Reasoning models now let users decide how long a model thinks before it answers, but we do not know what extra thinking does to such everyday inferences. We study this directly: we keep a model's weights fixed, change only how much it thinks, and record which reading it chooses. A second tool cuts the model's own reasoning at successive points and asks for an answer, showing where the reading changes. Thinking makes models read logical words as logic: it cancels the implicatures of some (not all) and or (not both) in most tested open reasoning models and in GPT-5, while context-driven inferences such as indirect answers improve. The trace shows why: models first entertain the enriched reading and cancel it later. Answering from that early reading, an exploratory inference-time remedy, recovers these implicatures without losing literal accuracy. Evaluations of reasoning models should measure how they interpret, not only how accurate they are.

title: ACE-Brain-0.6: Scaling Spatial Grounding for Physical Foundation Models

details.title: ACE-Brain-0.6: Scaling Spatial Grounding for Physical Foundation Models
details.abstract: General-purpose multimodal models, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5, demonstrate broad capabilities in embodied manipulation. Our analysis indicates that this generality is accompanied by strong spatial perception, as Astra can determine where to interact with task-relevant entities amid visual distractors. Because spatial perception connects high-level reasoning to the physical scene, we investigate scaling visual grounding to strengthen the perceptual foundation of general embodied operation. We develop a unified data pipeline that combines robot manipulation recordings with complementary visual data from diverse sources. After automatically annotating the robot recordings, the pipeline converts the collected data into verifiable grounding supervision. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on approximately 1.5 million samples produced by this pipeline yields ACE-Brain-0.6. The model outperforms GPT-6 Astra on four of seven public grounding benchmarks, with an overall average score of 75.41 compared with Astra's 73.68. Under a fixed Qwen3.5-9B fine-tuning setup, aggregate grounding performance improves steadily as successive data releases expand the training collection to cover a broader range of grounding scenarios. These results show that scaling verifiable grounding supervision from diverse sources can strengthen the spatial perception of an open 9B model for general embodied operation.

title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting

details.title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting
details.abstract: What does it take for AI agents to continuously improve themselves? We argue that the environment is not merely a place for training or evaluation, but a fundamental driver of recursive self-improvement (RSI). We introduce DeepEvolve, a system in which agents co-evolve with a living environment that continually generates new, verifiable real-world event prediction tasks, adapts to the agent’s weaknesses, and provides feedback for sustained capability growth. Through parameter-level learning and reusable skill evolution, DeepEvolve turns experience into lasting improvements while addressing information leakage in open-world learning. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements in real-world event prediction, highlighting evolving environments as a key foundation for self-improving AI.

title: CompactSplat: Spatially Adaptive Gaussian Distribution for Feedforward Scene Reconstruction

details.title: CompactSplat: Spatially Adaptive Gaussian Distribution for Feedforward Scene Reconstruction
details.abstract: Reconstructing 3D scenes from sparse views without per-scene optimization remains highly challenging, especially for recovering accurate geometry and fine textures. While recent feedforward approaches leverage generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for scene generation, they typically assign one or multiple Gaussians to each pixel. Such uniform allocation not only produces highly redundant representations by wasting primitives in homogeneous areas, but also fails to exploit the inherent geometric priors of planar surfaces, often resulting in sub-optimal structural modeling. To address these limitations, we present CompactSplat, a novel feedforward framework that enables a content-aware allocation of 3D Gaussians. By integrating texture-guided spatial partitioning with hierarchical sampling, CompactSplat adaptively distributes primitives — concentrating dense Gaussians in complex regions while tiling flat areas with expanded, scale-modulated primitives. Moreover, our framework inherently supports dynamic sparsity control at inference time, enabling seamless trade-offs between rendering fidelity and memory footprint without requiring network retraining. Extensive experiments on RealEstate10K, DL3DV, and ScanNet demonstrate that CompactSplat consistently outperforms prior methods on both standard metrics and high-resolution rendering consistency, achieving high-fidelity reconstructions with significantly fewer primitives.

title: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training

details.title: Answering in the User's Variety: Calibrated Accommodation Pairs for Post-Training
details.abstract: People adapt how they talk to the person in front of them. However, chat models tend to respond in Standard English regardless of the dialect used by the user. A uniform answer can hide whether training treats these users alike, and output audits cannot tell as well. We trace how each post-training stage, from supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to preference optimization (DPO) and reinforcement learning, changes a model's tendency to match the user, and read what each update prefers from two content-matched replies, one matching the user and one not. Across 10 open model lineages, post-training standardizes replies to every informal cue, yet after adjusting for how likely each reply already was, the DPO update still favours matching British and Australian spelling over AAE and Singlish on 10 lineages, and models still produce AAE features when asked. We then introduce calibrated accommodation pairs (CAP), preference data that reward matching users' dialect density while preserving Standard English for Standard-English users. On a fully open model, CAP raises convergence on features it was not trained on without a detectable increase in dialect for Standard-English users or a cost in instruction following. In contrast, one-sided pairs reach a similar gain only by overshooting the user and imposing dialect. Our findings show that uniform replies can hide selective updates and audits should read the update as well as the output.

details.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift
details.abstract: Perimeter triage faces a latency/semantics trade-off: signature engines are fast and format-safe but blind to unseen attacks, while generative models are semantic but slow and produce unparseable output. In late 2026 a class of commercial System One decision models (TypeSafe Jev; Microsoft-Decision-1) began selling typed decision primitives - binary gates, closed-set choices, ordinal scores - as product APIs, with no academic treatment. We present VX-One: a small multi-head network (100K-10M parameters) whose outputs are these primitives - a calibrated gate, a choice over a closed candidate set that always includes an explicit unknown option, and an ordinal score, trained multi-task, temperature-calibrated per head (~0.7-1.7 ms p50 on CPU). We evaluate it on UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, EMBER2024 against calibrated XGBoost, Random-Forest, MLP, Kitsune, and measure a two-phase cascade (Suricata with 52,674 Emerging-Threats rules -> VX-One) over five days of CIC-IDS2017. Findings: (i) VX-One wins detection (AUROC/FPR@95%TPR) on UNSW-NB15 and under temporal drift on CIC-IDS2017 (0.711 vs 0.637), but XGBoost wins multi-class attribution on all three benchmarks; (ii) leave-one-family-out gate detects never-seen families on 9/9 UNSW folds yet drops below chance on CIC recon family, and abstention threshold transfers poorly across benchmarks; (iii) on payload-less reconstructions signature engines resolve ~0.1% of flows - gray zone ~99.9% of traffic, recovered by Phase 2 (combined recall >=0.978); (iv) calibration collapses under temporal drift (ECE 0.04->0.40) for every method while ranking partially survives. We provide a measured account of where typed calibrated decisions help perimeter triage, and where they fail.

title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation

details.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
details.abstract: Cinematic video generation requires both temporal inference from limited inputs (i.e., sparse rather than frame-by-frame guidance) and factor-aware control of character, scene, action, and camera. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer useful priors for both capabilities, but their representations are not automatically actionable for video generation: a Video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) may bypass them through native conditioning pathways, and using them does not ensure either factor-aware control or generation-compatible temporal prediction. We propose Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL), which establishes effective MLLM latent use as a shared prerequisite and then targets the two capabilities with complementary learning signals. First, latent-only generator grounding trains the DiT with a frozen MLLM and connector, strengthening the DiT's use of MLLM latents for generation. Second, for factor-aware control, paired videos specify a target-factor change and non-target preservation, and factor-span replacement trains the DiT to realize this relationship in its output. Third, for temporal inference, text-only and text-plus-complete-video observations share a video target, and the trained DiT is then frozen while the MLLM and connector are optimized through it. This final stage trains limited-input representations for generation while retaining complete-observation reconstruction as a complementary training mode. Extensive experiments demonstrate our consistently better performance on three cinematic video generation tasks (i.e., sparse-to-video, factor-aware editing, and multi-shot generation) over baselines and validate FAPL's contributions to MLLM feature use, temporal control, and factor coordination.

title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation

details.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
details.abstract: We introduce LayerEditor , a unified framework that couples instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers. Given a source image, an editing instruction, and a requested layer count, LayerEditor jointly generates an edited canvas and an ordered RGBA layer stack, enabling explicit control over individual layer content. In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling. LayerEditor jointly represents the edited canvas and ordered RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, with appearance and opacity modeled as distinct, interacting fields. Shared attention captures dependencies between the canvas and layer stack, while layer-aware rotary coordinates encode field identity and stacking order while preserving spatial correspondence. This formulation supports variable layer counts within a shared architecture. Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation (C-EPD). To preserve the pretrained model’s editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, C-EPD queries a frozen editing teacher at intermediate states along the student’s own denoising trajectory. It combines direct-output velocity matching with pixel-space supervision of the image composed from the predicted RGBA layers. Gradients propagate through decoding and alpha compositing, transferring the pretrained editing prior to both the edited canvas and the layered output. LayerEditor-100K and dedicated benchmarks. We construct LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale paired image-editing dataset containing 100K examples, each with a source image, an editing instruction, an edited target, and an ordered RGBA stack of 2–10 layers. We further introduce Crello-Testset and ScaleEdit-Testset to evaluate editing fidelity, layer quality, and controllability over layer count and user-specified layer content.

title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI

details.title: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
details.abstract: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks for more than a better robot: the process that produces improvements should itself get better. Digital agents already rewrite their own code and check each version against executable tests. But what does it take to carry these mechanisms into the physical world, where feedback is partial, trials are costly, and some mistakes cannot be undone? What the paper covers: 🧭 A ladder of claims : behavioral improvement → later-learning benefit → procedure improvement → recursion. Each step is defined by the comparison that would establish it. 🤖 Where improvement lands : policies, world models, external knowledge (skills, code, memory), the learning procedure, and the improver that revises it. 🔁 When gains carry forward : four conditions. Feedback addresses the remaining need, the receiving component can use the change, the change stays useful under task or hardware shift, and practice remains safe and affordable. 📍 Where the field stands : existing robot studies show behavioral improvement, later-learning benefits, and procedure improvement, but none yet isolates a gain attributable to recursion. 🧪 What's still open : fair tests the system can't overfit to, gains that keep stacking up, safe practice while the procedure changes, and what a first real demo of physical RSI would need to show. 🌐 Project page: https://physical2rsi.github.io/ 💻 Paper list: https://github.com/Physical2RSI/Awesome-Physical2RSI Feedback and pointers to work we missed are very welcome!

title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models

details.title: Deep Fusion Memory: A Chunk-Level Parametric Memory for Large Language Models
details.abstract: We introduce Deep Fusion Memory (DFM) , a chunk-level parametric memory architecture that enables LLMs to incorporate external knowledge without retrieval at inference time. DFM introduces two key ideas: Efficient memory construction: A causal memory predictor learns from retrieved chunk embeddings, reducing retrieval queries by 32× and retrieved items by 2048× during training data construction. Deep memory fusion: Predicted memory is integrated into intermediate hidden states through gated cross-attention, while keeping the LLM backbone frozen. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across knowledge-intensive QA and domain adaptation tasks. We hope this work offers a scalable and efficient direction for equipping LLMs with external parametric memory. Feedback and discussions are welcome!

title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions

details.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
details.abstract: TL;DR A La nguage-conditioned La tent World model ( LaLa-World ) uses natural language as a shared action interface to learn from simulation, robotics, images, and videos. It predicts future visual representations for efficient planning across domains and can be fine-tuned into LaLa-Policy , which jointly predicts robot actions and future representations. Key results: One LaLa-World predictor trained across domains beats per-domain LWMs on average MPC planning performance Adding image/video data further improves planning and robustness to action phrasing vs. an RAEv2-based video generation baseline: comparable planning with 6× less training cost and 13.9× faster planning LaLa-Policy , initialized from LaLa-World, is competitive with Cosmos Policy on LIBERO and RoboCasa with up to 5.5× faster inference Project page: https://june-page.github.io/lala-world/ Code: https://github.com/junha1125/LaLa-World alphaXiv: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2610.27851 arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27851 Presentation: https://june-page.github.io/lala-world-slides/

title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models

details.title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
details.abstract: 🚀 We are excited to share our latest work: "What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models" ! Unified multimodal models (UMMs) can generate images with rich visual details. But can the internal representations underlying their generation capabilities also help improve fine-grained multimodal understanding? Existing generation-assisted understanding methods primarily rely on generative supervision or explicitly generated intermediate outputs, while the potential of native generation-side representations remains largely unexplored. We aim to investigate whether these representations can be leveraged to enhance fine-grained visual understanding. To this end, we systematically investigate the visual representations of generation and understanding pathways in UMMs. Building on our findings, we introduce GAFU (Generation-Assisted Fine-grained Understanding) , a post-training framework that directly leverages native generation-side representations to enhance fine-grained visual understanding. 🔑 Key Highlights 🔍 Systematic Investigation: We systematically compare generation-side and understanding-side representations across six UMMs, revealing key properties in fine-grained semantic sensitivity, representational complementarity, and spatial dependence . Our findings show that generation-side representations are more sensitive to fine-grained semantic changes and capture visual variations that are less effectively reflected in understanding-side representations, with these advantages closely tied to spatial organization. 🧩 GAFU Framework: We propose a post-training framework that leverages native generation-side representations without requiring explicit image generation at inference. GAFU compresses and aligns generation-side features into compact G tokens , enables task-conditioned retrieval and injection of complementary information, and incorporates pairwise preference learning to encourage effective utilization of generation-side representations. 📈 Extensive Experimental Validation: We evaluate GAFU across three unified multimodal architectures (BAGEL, Janus-Pro, and Lance) and five benchmarks covering general, spatial, and domain-specific understanding. GAFU consistently outperforms matched-data SFT baselines across all 15 model–benchmark combinations , achieving  up to 20.00%, 17.94%, and 8.62% relative improvements on VStar-Bench, OmniSpatial, and VSR-Bench, respectively. Our findings demonstrate that the generation capabilities of UMMs are valuable not only for producing visual content but also for providing complementary representations that enhance fine-grained visual understanding, opening up new opportunities for synergy between understanding and generation. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23987 💻 Code: https://github.com/LRuca/GAFU We welcome feedback and discussions!

title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE

details.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
details.abstract: A comparison between the Vanilla and Meta-Expert models shows that, when trained under the optimal settings of the Vanilla model at varying depths and scales, models with Meta Experts achieve loss comparable to the Vanilla baselines while using only 70–80% as many experts, or 75–90% as many parameters. Notably, the savings in both experts and parameters grow as the models become deeper and larger, demonstrating the favorable scalability of Meta Experts. The proposed method has been scaled up in Intern-S2-Mobius, which is available at https://github.com/InternLM/Intern-S2-Mobius and https://huggingface.co/internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius .

title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents

details.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
details.abstract: Tool-using voice agents often leave users waiting after speech ends, even when actionable information arrives earlier in the request. Speculative approaches begin work during speech, but chunk-bounded or interrupt-on-update generation can truncate a tool call before its arguments are complete. This couples computation time to speech updates, limiting useful work completed in advance. We introduce Heartbeat Thinking, which handles updated input through new Thinker invocations while allowing ongoing invocations and dispatched tools to finish. Periodic invocations read the latest partial transcript and a shared record of completed reasoning and tool results. These results help resolve missing arguments and initiate dependent calls, allowing preparation to progress across speech updates. Across SpeechFCEval, FDBench v3, and AudioCRAG, Heartbeat improves aggregate speculative tool coverage or retrieval reuse over a SHANKS-style windowed baseline, with benchmark-dependent effects on final task quality. On FDBench v3, it increases tool coverage by 16 percentage points and reduces mean final-response latency by 36.4%. The results show that heartbeat thinking paradigm preserving ongoing computation during speech can turn listening time into reusable preparation for faster and more capable voice-agent responses.

title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V

details.title: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
details.abstract: We introduce Code2Video-Compass, a comprehensive benchmark for general-purpose code-based video generation across text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video settings. The benchmark comprises 2,104 tasks spanning 10 categories and 24 subtypes, covering scene construction, dynamic animation, and state dependency. We evaluate 15 MLLMs using complementary objective metrics and MLLM-based judgments, revealing substantial performance gaps across input settings and task complexities, as well as a disconnect between visual quality and execution reliability. We welcome feedback and discussion!

title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation

details.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re excited to share Cola2, a follow-up to Cola that combines dynamic semantic compression with joint learning of continuous representations and discrete text generation. With a Qwen-initialized decoder, Cola2 surpasses Llama-3-8B on HellaSwag and StoryCloze after just 346B additional training tokens, while still unconverged. We plan to open-source the 8B model in the coming weeks. Feedback and discussion are very welcome! Project page: https://hongcanguo.github.io/Cola2/

title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

details.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
details.abstract: We present RLSplat , a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method that enables resource-aware inference through direct Gaussian budget control. By generating exactly the requested number of Gaussians, RLSplat allows users to adapt inference cost to their available computational resources. Unlike existing methods that generate an oversized Gaussian representation and prune it afterward, RLSplat directly generates a representation within the target budget. In zero-shot evaluations, it outperforms prior budget-controllable methods across the tested budgets, achieving up to 4.1× faster inference and 9.6× lower peak memory in low-budget settings.

title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing

details.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
details.abstract: LLM routing dynamically selects and coordinates heterogeneous language models across diverse tasks. However, existing approaches are largely built around a predefined execution paradigm, such as single-round, multi-round, or agentic routing, which fixes how model calls are organized and limits adaptation to different query needs. We propose RouteWeaver, a unified routing framework that integrates these routing modes within a single LLM policy, jointly learning which mode to use and how to select models within that mode. To jointly optimize mode selection and within-mode execution, we develop COMET-GRPO (COordinated Mode–Execution Training), which decouples the trajectory-level advantage into separate signals for mode selection and within-mode execution, enabling more targeted credit assignment to each decision level. We further introduce progressive exploration, which gradually shifts training from externally assigned modes to autonomous selection, so that the router first learns how to execute each mode before deciding when to use it. We evaluate RouteWeaver across mathematics, coding, knowledge, logical reasoning, and factual recall. RouteWeaver achieves an average accuracy of 61.4%, an 11.03% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, and outperforms all compared baselines in each of the five domains. Ablations show that both COMET-GRPO and progressive exploration are important for adaptive routing; without progressive exploration, the routing policy collapses entirely to single-round execution.

title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks

details.title: Policy-Mask: Budget-Aware Adaptation of Diffusion Features to Discriminative Tasks
details.abstract: TLDR: Policy-Mask trains a REINFORCE policy that jointly picks the timestep, layer, and exactly b channels of a frozen diffusion model, then distills the selected features into a student that runs without the teacher. At 128 of 1280 channels, it beats full-width features from a fixed (t, l) by 1.2–1.6 mIoU on four segmentation benchmarks and outperforms RepFusion.

title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models

details.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
details.abstract: We introduce FRED , a framework that trains World Action Models (WAMs) to generate better future video representations in a single denoising step, by self-distilling from noisy ground-truth futures and conditioning on short history observations. FRED outperforms competing WAMs across real-world manipulation, with especially large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks. On robot tasks demonstrated only in human videos, it reaches 50.0% success rate vs. 19.4% for the best competing WAM. 🤗 Models: https://huggingface.co/collections/FRED-AGI-LAB/fred-6adad8ae754754e2f2f1afa7

title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos

details.title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos
details.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made synthetic videos increasingly realistic, placing greater demands on reliable AI-generated video detection. Existing artifact-based detectors typically identify generation artifacts as evidence for source prediction, yet they may either fail to recognize subtle artifacts or reach the correct source decision without faithfully identifying the evidence underlying it. In this work, we systematically investigate how to design and train effective artifact detectors and formulate artifact detection as a structured process comprising three complementary capabilities: Inspection Planning, which determines what should be examined; Evidence Verification, which verifies whether the inspected content exhibits genuine generation artifacts; and Evidence Aggregation, which integrates the verified evidence into the final source decision. Building on this formulation, we introduce Verus-Insight, trained with human-anchored full-process supervision and progressive capability training to strengthen both fine-grained artifact detection and video-level detection. We further introduce Verus-Bench, a benchmark with fine-grained human annotations of perceptible artifacts for evaluating artifact detection. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate that Verus-Insight achieves strong performance in both fine-grained artifact analysis and AI-generated video detection, with substantial gains in recovering human-perceived artifacts. Further analyses reveal that the three capabilities are complementary yet distinct, and that Verus-Insight more reliably converts relevant inspection targets into supported artifact evidence without increasing spurious artifact claims.

title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression

details.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression

It shows strong empirical gains both as a compressor for block-wise sparse attention in efficient LLMs and as a VL projector (merger) in MLLMs. Beyond that, it opens up many exciting applications to explore: temporal compression for video/audio, training natively efficient ViTs from scratch, depth-wise compression for better depth scaling...

title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought

details.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
details.abstract: RAW-RAG challenges the necessity of complex agentic memory for long-term conversation understanding. By combining dense retrieval and reranking over raw history, it ranks first among compared memory systems in six of seven settings across four benchmarks. Its analyses highlight evidence coverage and relational completeness as key drivers of performance, establishing naive RAG as an essential baseline.

title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation

details.title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation
details.abstract: We introduce RTAformer , accepted at ACCV 2026, for Video Scene Graph Generation (VidSGG). Existing temporal models often retain outdated relation predictions even after the underlying relationships change. We identify this failure mode as Relational Semantic Inertia . RTAformer addresses this issue by disentangling entity persistence from relation dynamics, using calibrated relation-query differences to guide predicate updates and cross-frame instance alignment to stabilize temporal representations. Experiments on Action Genome demonstrate improved performance, with particularly strong gains on relation-transition frames under matched-backbone comparisons. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20091 Code (coming soon): https://github.com/sejong-rcv/RTAformer

title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding

details.title: AgentVQA: A Unified Benchmark for Agentic Visual Understanding
details.abstract: AgentVQA is an offline benchmark for evaluating visual understanding in realistic agentic scenarios, without the cost of running agents in interactive environments. It brings together 1,000 human-verified examples from 23 datasets across five domains: web agents, robotics, egocentric videos, games, and spatial planning. Our evaluation of 22 VLMs reveals substantial limitations in visual grounding, motion understanding, state tracking, and spatial reasoning. Importantly, model rankings on AgentVQA also align with corresponding online evaluations, supporting its use as a scalable alternative for assessing agentic visual understanding.

title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark

details.title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark
details.abstract: AI coding agents can now build small playable games in minutes, but the results usually look like programmer art: gray blockouts, colored geometric primitives, and flat semantic blobs. We present AnyGameRenderer, a video-to-video generative renderer that turns such footage into high-quality visuals with characters, motion detail, and effects. Throughout, it keeps the layout, camera, and every entity's position and timing intact. Our AnyGameRenderer generalizes across a wide range of genres that agents build, such as tower defense, auto-battlers, top-down survivors, turn-based battles, kart racing, and crowd runners. AnyGameRenderer takes plain video as its game-state input, with no complex representations such as engine G-buffers, per-object class labels, or low-poly proxies. Gray blockouts, colored primitives, semantic maps, and wireframes all work as input. It also preserves entity correspondence: group counts stay correct, and entities appear and disappear on the right frame. We implement AnyGameRenderer by LoRA fine-tuning MiniMax-H3 ref2va, a 33B reference-video-conditioned video generation model. Training uses ∼10k paired clips from three sources: (i) multi-stream rendering data from 38 agent-made games exported from GEAR, an AI game-creation tool; (ii) two-stream rendering data from Unreal Engine, with programmatically controlled crowds, count changes, and entity scales; and (iii) real gameplay recordings, with pairs reconstructed via 3D-box detection. To evaluate the entity correspondence, we propose an entity-level benchmark of 59 held-out cases with 753 entities, scored against ground-truth boxes. Compared with the base model, AnyGameRenderer better preserves entity correspondence: temporal match rises from 50.9% to 62.9%, missed count changes fall from 34.7% to 21.3%, and fewer entities are hallucinated or left unrendered.

title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning

details.title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning
details.abstract: MolLean turns chemical reasoning into executable, checked steps. Direct chain-of-thought can miscount atoms, invent functional groups, or claim a property improved without measuring it. MolLean ties declared edits and claims to an explicit molecular state. The video illustrates four examples from the paper: ethanol-to-1-propanol editing, an exact 25-carbon constraint, QED optimization with measured feedback, and an interactive MolLean-MCP episode where a rejected phenyl attachment leaves the molecule unchanged and guides the next successful action. Across 8,800 matched examples covering 12 chemical task types, whole-trace refinement improves over direct CoT on all 12 with Qwen3.6-27B. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20459 Project preview: https://github.com/phenixace/Open-MolLean Code release is planned.

title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation

details.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
details.abstract: We’re sharing F2G-Pose, accepted at NeurIPS 2026! From a single segmented RGB-D observation, it predicts category-level 6D object pose, metric size, and a completed shape in the camera frame in one forward pass. It lifts frozen foundation visual features into 3D and fuses them with local geometry through a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. No instance-specific CAD models or reference views are required. The paper reports 28 FPS for pose-only model inference under its benchmark protocol. Code, pretrained weights, and a 90-second demo are available. Happy to discuss the method and results! Pretrained weights: https://huggingface.co/J3rr1/F2G-Pose

title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models

details.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models
details.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is credited with teaching reasoning models to write {wait} before reconsidering a step, yet large RL accuracy gains do not require the word. This view can confuse what RL discovers with what a model inherits from its training data. We trace the word through open models' training histories, reading it with label-free indices of frequency, position, form and usage and an injected-error test, all computed from sampled outputs. We find that zero-RL almost never coins the marker: on bases that lack the word, RL raises MATH-500 accuracy substantially while {wait} stays near absent. It arrives with training data: mid-training in OLMo-3, and fine-tuning on reasoning traces installs it in most models whose base lacks it. Where the base already uses it, both released RL-Zero recipes (OLMo-3, MiMo) multiply it, whereas KL-free GRPO from the same base does not; OLMo-3's recipe wears down its form and makes it a more sensitive but more liberal alarm; RL after supervised fine-tuning barely changes it, and our GRPO recipe erases a marker seeded by fine-tuning. Finally, we show that marker frequency alone does not indicate RL-induced reasoning and caution against LLM-as-a-judge revision metrics, as automated judges can reverse human-labelled trends.

title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research

details.title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research
details.abstract: What if AI could actually do scientific research, not just generate ideas or write papers? Excited to share SplatLab (NeurIPS 2026) , an autonomous AI scientist for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Starting from a single prompt (or no prompt at all) SplatLab autonomously reads research papers, reproduces published methods, proposes novel improvements, implements code, runs real GPU experiments, performs ablations, and writes complete research manuscripts. Key results: 🧪 16 research manuscripts generated end-to-end without human code edits. 📈 Up to +3.78 dB PSNR over reproduced baselines in evaluated experiments. ⚡ 24–48 hours for an autonomous research run. 🔍 Verifiable science: Every reported numerical result is traced to an actual experiment log. Unlike AI systems that only propose hypotheses, SplatLab closes the loop from scientific ideas to experimentally validated discoveries. We've open-sourced the framework, generated manuscripts, and experimental records. We'd love feedback from the community!

title: MambaAct: Efficient Mamba Action Experts for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models

details.title: MambaAct: Efficient Mamba Action Experts for Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 We're excited to share MambaAct , an efficient action expert for flow-matching VLAs. Flow-matching VLAs like π0.5 run their action expert many times during denoising, which makes inference a bottleneck for real-time control. MambaAct keeps π0.5's pretrained vision-language encoder but replaces the transformer action expert with a compact Mamba-based one. A lightweight Context Compressor turns the VLM tokens into a compact conditioning signal, so we avoid repeated token-level cross-attention. 🚀 Key results: 10× smaller action expert 64.8% lower denoising latency on LIBERO, 58.8% on a real robot +1.08 pp mean success on LIBERO (3 seeds), with gains maintained on LIBERO-Plus and real-world tasks 💻 Code: https://github.com/giakhuyendihoc/MambaAct Weight will be released soon!
